title: Polyglot pin interpretation and strictness levels
creator: Amina Patel
description: Clarify and implement a unified model version pin resolution strategy across API and SDKs that supports multiple pin types (human tags, semver and semver ranges, commit hashes) and introduces a configurable strictness level. The goal is predictable resolution, clear developer ergonomics, and correct binding of performance profiles to concrete model artifacts. This work touches model onboarding, catalog publishing, runtime resolver, SDK helpers, and docs + migration guidance.
background: Current behavior is inconsistent across clients: some SDKs accept a tag string and resolve server-side to whatever 'latest' means, others try semver ranges client-side, and performance profiles are published at per-release granularity that doesn't always map to user pins. This causes surprising runtime fallbacks and mismatched performance expectations in production workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document canonical precedence for pin forms: exact commit hash > exact semver > semver range > tag alias > floating alias (e.g., 'latest')
Add a 'pin_strictness' option (enum: strict|lenient|fail_fast) available in API request header and SDK constructors
When strict: resolution only returns exact matches for hash or semver; tag aliases are rejected if they don't resolve to a concrete semver or commit on the server
When lenient: allow best-effort resolution according to precedence and return resolution metadata in response headers for auditing
When fail_fast: if a pin cannot be resolved to a concrete artifact, server returns 409 with guidance; no runtime fallback occurs

Performance profiles are published and versioned per model artifact (commit hash + semver) and the serving runtime uses the profile matching the resolved artifact; when resolving to a tag, the profile attached to the concrete artifact used must be surfaced
SDKs expose helper utilities: Pin.parse(), Pin.normalize(), and warnings for ambiguous pins; unit and integration tests cover these helpers
Rollout plan and docs updated with migration guidance and a 3-month deprecation schedule for ambiguous tag behavior
E2E test matrix covers Dedicated, Hosted, and Private deployments and verifies consistent resolution and profile application across modes
notes: Design trade-offs: server-side resolution centralizes policy but increases control-plane load; client-side pre-resolution reduces server calls but risks divergence between client heuristics and server catalog state. We'll adopt server-side authoritative resolution with SDK helpers for local validation.
We will store resolution metadata in request traces and token-level cost dashboards to help customers debug unexpected fallbacks or performance regressions.

Edge cases to handle: semver pre-release identifiers, build metadata (ignored for precedence), and tags that map to multiple artifacts across model families (must be rejected unless explicit model-family context provided).
We should design the runtime to prefer precomputed mapping tables (alias -> artifact) for high-traffic aliases like 'redwood-base-latest' to avoid heavy lookup costs.
Performance profile publishing: require publisher to attach profile to a specific artifact_id (commit hash) and optionally to a semver; publishing UI/API will show 'applies to' mapping.
implementation_plan: Spec: formalize resolution precedence and strictness semantics and add to API spec
Server: implement resolution service that returns resolved_artifact, resolution_reason, and profile_id; surface via X-Resolved-Artifact and X-Resolution-Reason headers
Runtime: bind performance profile to resolved_artifact rather than to incoming pin string
SDKs: add Pin helpers, default strictness = lenient, expose header opt-in for fail_fast
Docs: update onboarding guide, pinning migration doc, and performance profile publishing page
QA: add integration tests for all combinations of pin types and strictness levels across environments
Migration: create a confluence doc and email cadence to notify existing customers of upcoming stricter behavior and suggested action steps
risks: Customers rely on current ambiguous 'latest' semantics and may experience broken workloads under strict mode
Increased control plane load for server-side resolution if alias tables are not cached or precomputed
Complexity in UI/console to display which performance profile was applied when tags are used
mitigations: Default to lenient for the initial rollout and provide an opt-in header/SDK flag for strict/fail_fast
Add caching/eager alias materialization for popular tags; instrument cache hit rate and fallbacks
Console: surface 'resolved artifact' next to model pins in request logs and provide a 'why' link that points to the profile used
Provide a migration CLI to enumerate usages of ambiguous tags in a customer's account and suggest semver or hash replacements
